recipes.name: Healthier Delicious Ham and Potato Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon ground white pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Combine potatoes, carrots, green beans, celery, onion, ham, and water in a stockpot. Bring to a boil and cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Stir in chicken bouillon and pepper.

Melt butter in a separate saucepan over medium-low heat. Whisk in flour with a fork and cook, stirring constantly, until thick, about 1 minute. Slowly stir in milk so lumps do not form until all of the milk has been added. Continue stirring until thick, 4 to 5 minutes.
Pour milk mixture into the stockpot and cook soup until heated through, about 5 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Delicious Ham and Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: With added carrots and green beans, and using non-fat milk, this healthier version of ham-and-potato soup turns out great every time.

review.reviewBody: I have always liked the original version of this recipe and I liked this too, but I don't know how much 'healthier' it is. I used about 4 large carrots and a whole smallish onion - a lot more celery than is called for. Add what ever vegetables you have available. This is one of those great comfort meals - enjoy but don't think it is that much 'healthier'.

This was very popular with my family. I did not have any ham, so for bulk I added mushrooms, sauteeing them first, then adding the rest of the ingredients. I used 1/2 full fat milk and half 1% milk, reducing the calories somewhat, but also adding some richness. I used Better Than Boullion and doubled the recipe and ended up with a ton of soup, which was great. This is an excellent potato soup recipe, the definitive one for clean eating. Loved it.

My husband and two kids all really liked this soup. I didn't even add the milk/flour. I found that once I used a masher to mash up the potatoes, the soup was plenty thick and creamy. Also I used a spiral ham that had enough salt, so I skipped the bouillon. I added fresh dill and parsley too. So with less salt and no milk, it was even healthier/low calorie.

I used this for a base as I changed a few things. First I halved the recipe, I didn't need this much. Had no green bean. I did make a base with chicken broth and cauliflower, then purified it. Then did the potatoes, carrots, onion, ham and celery as directed. Once that was hot, I added the cauliflower mix. Continued to heat as directed, did the butter, flour and skim milk and added to the bigger pot. I have to admit I added some cheddar cheese, so I probably took away some of the healthiness. But this was very good. I only gave it a 4 because I didn't follow exactly.
Great soup and quick to make! I used chicken broth instead of water and added corn, carrots and ground turkey instead of ham. My family loved it! Thank you!

I did not use the butter, milk, or flour. I used vegetable and chicken stock, increased the carrot, green beans, and onion. For seasonings, I added a little allspice and Marsalla. Really tasty. Jane.Braun

Love this reciepe. Been making it for years I was hoping to get a healthier version without loss of flavor. I don't think this did it. I sauté onions veggies, ham and ham bone first. Then add chicken stock or bullion with water. Make sure to cook the butter an flour in separate pan before adding that keeps the pasty flavor away. Bone really helps with flavor as the sauté does. Enjoy your comfort dish not a healthy version good try

I made this for my family last night. The only thing I left off were the green beans. For the Ham I used a Ham Bone I had in the freezer. My family thought this was wonderful and there was not any left! The only added thing I did was use my immersible blender to blend it a bit.
I made this without the dairy and flour - it was great! I was surprised by how spicy it turned out to be. Usually add extra pepper but am glad I stuck to the recipe for that.
Followed the recipe but made it non dairy by using vegan butter and coconut milk. Delicious!
It was a little bland at first. I added salt, pepper, chicken stock, and crushed red pepper. I would make it again, but would work on adding more flavor. Texture was perfect, it was very creamy!

This recipe is now over 13 years old! Congrats on lasting so long! I still consider it bland but I have used it as my "go to" template for using up leftover ham. To perk this recipe up several notches, I add a few jalapeno peppers, with seeds and membranes removed and discarded, and I add a few garlic cloves, and I add bacon! Why? Well because everything tastes better with bacon!
Good flavor without heavy seasoning. All the veggies were great with some time saved by using frozen cut green beans, and also used extra amounts of the other veggies.
I have been making this soup for over 10 years now . It is an easy tasty soup.
My wife and I made this recipe today. It was quick and easy to make and did not disappoint! Very delicious.
Sooo good. Leftover frozen spiral ham from Christmas, all the other ingredients plus a can of creamed corn, it is so tasty!
Great as is.
Very good. So much better than my old recipe. I used a cup of frozen mixed vegetables to replace carrots and green beans, so I had peas and corn in the soup but it was colorful. Nice.
Very easy to make. Amazing recipe. Will definitely make this again. My family really loved this.

It was delicious. Only problem is that it took way longer to cook because I had to keep whisking in more flour and then corn starch, as others did, to thicken the sauce. I will make adjustments in the beginning to speed it up.
